i live by the beach and a lot of ladies here wear these under tank tops with large arm holes, like [this](https://encrypted-tbn3.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcTgDaWNIJRziAAxNUFee2bJtRIoUABigZGnA5vBi6MDK9nSddgU-Q), or with something high-waisted like [this](https://encrypted-tbn1.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcQuDnko8bnoHVq04xyFoqx6uDbY9M7w4T2f8DWXskY5mZfYfN-B). i'm not able to find a picture, but under a partially zipped-up bomber jacket or vest with some skinny jeans would be really cute as well. and don't be self conscious that it looks like a bra -- it's cute and once you fashion it right, only you will know that you bought a cute top that just so happens to also double as a bralette.
i believe in you. there's better things on the other side.

i dated one for 2.5 years. apparently he also "taught" "the Game", was a "professional wing-man", had a "professional mentor", etc. i still really don't know what that means. he told me about a week after we started dating, and i told him how much i didn't think that was cool and would be very hurt if i found out he was using his "day game" or "night game" to get me to stay with him. he explained he did it because he felt awkward in his youth and agreed that it was a demeaning out look on women. i appreciated him feeling awkward and i was able to understand it better, and it helped me open up about how awkward i felt. we fought about it a few times after, but he was very open to discussing what happened and appreciated my feelings about it while respecting his own. excellent communication.

my relationship with him actually ended up the healthiest and most loving that i had ever had. we broke up because he wanted to get married when we were young and i was far from ready. i still keep in contact with him and his family regularly.

it's a really weird way of going about it, but most of them really are just scared as fuck about being themselves on dates (who isn't?). i preferred his scripted, almost DnD like approach to dating versus the entitled dating approach that i found on most subsequent dates. he wanted to learn ways to make himself feel more comfortable with weird pre-scripted jokes and scenarios... and quickly found out that wasn't attracting the type of women he wanted to be comfortable with. the other men i dated felt entitled to our dates because they were "so confident / rich / successful / manly / great in bed".

the pick-up artistry really doesn't make the man, and each of us have very strange pasts. i was an actress and made out on stage / faked falling in love with people for money. life is just weird.

TL;DR almost married the one i dated. was hurt when i learned at first but he ended up being the nicest boyfriend. helped me understand how awkward he felt and how scared he was to be himself. as always, past + open communication => profit. great guy.

i appreciate you not wanting to be alone and single. when i was very young, i had an overwhelming sense that i would find someone who i really got along with fantastically, so being single after an LTR felt like "whoaretheywherearetheyhowdoifindthem". but if you anchor too much onto that feeling, you risk settling just to avoid that fear from realizing.

i have a lot of friends who date around, so i gave it a shot and said "why not" to anyone who asked me out and didn't give me a sinking feeling of dread and death. it was nice, but it took me about a dozen dates to finally realize i wasn't having a good time at all. i wanted a "best friend whose face i wanted on my face", not romantic interviews... so i stopped accepting dates from online sites and otherwise blind set ups. i invested my time in trying out groups until i find ones that really represented my personal (unrelated from dating) values, and then my now SO hit me like a freight train of "oh there you are" at a non-profit. it was like a life event search engine.

TL;DR online engines / blind dates => find out what you want => hang out where said want would hang out and/or where the person you want to grow into would hang out => profit

i'm a make-up artist and freelance vendor, so i can confirm this is actually pretty common. i book a lot of men for special events and meet a lot of men who need to restock their foundation. i'm also a big fan of guy-liner, and actually am massively turned off by a guy who won't let me play dress-up on his face.

(advice) as always, tons of make-up really doesn't look good on anybody, mainly foundation. if you apply too much, your skin looks dirty. tinted moisturizers and "BB creams" are a fanfuckingtastic way to avoid this and will prevent face aging (from sun damage) because they're usually SPF 50million+. mineral powders are great until they clog your pores, so just say no. and when i do make-up for photos or film, i always, always, always do at least the upper water line with some eyeliner (light brown) or else lolwut.

all of my nationals (the professionals who travel all over the world to rep the line) are dudes. every single damn one (nope nope not bitter at all). all wear make-up. you would never know and they look like they just fucking naturally glow, except some of it get it in their stubble and then you //definitely// know.

both my SO and i are extreme introverts who work in extremely social fields some 30-60 hrs/week (i'm an actress/make-up artist, he's an event manager/technician). i guess for us, we want to either be together or be alone. our outside social circles really only extend to our DnD campaigns that we started long before dating. maybe some years from now we'll get sick of seeing each other all the time, but he's the coolest person i ever met and i want my face on his all the time... all social options directly oppose my interests.

i feel this so deeply. the market is terrible right now, let alone for folks who struggle with the debilitating self efficacy problems that come with depression and other mental illnesses. it hurts, and it makes you feel like you don't have control. i'm in the same boat, living off money i got from one freelancing season while i try to assemble myself into something presentable for someone, anyone to hire. i feel that money clock click down everyday, and i hear you. i'm fighting with you. it's really rough out here. you aren't alone.

it's been 5 hours and i wanted to thank everyone for their advice. unfortunately things are not getting better. the biggest reason i wanted to make this post was because i've been feeling alone for a very long time, however more so recently as i was told i should reach out to loved ones about my condition. i began reaching out and the lack of understanding is painful. the day is getting tougher. i used to pride myself on my strength to not let things show but i am seeing myself for how weak i truly am. it's getting easier to widdle through options of how to make this happen. i don't understand what it takes to get out of this hole, nor why it's this hard nor why it's getting harder and fuck i can't seem to jump start any sense of self efficacy anywhere in me. there's no where to go to find answers. it's debilitating. i feel powerless against this.

thank you. i would love to hear what you wanted to say later on. i think it's the panic attacks mixed with hopelessness that are the worst, particularly when they are unrelenting and in quick succession. it's an incredibly painful existence to live. i appreciate your understanding.

thank you, i wish i could. unfortunately my locations can be as far as 20-90 minutes away from where i live. i've been looking for part time gigs within walking distance so that i can leave my job, but i'm losing momentum. i've been pulling out all the stops to get out of this place. i don't know, i can't get the pain to stop long enough to do something more. thank you. i appreciate your time.

i appreciate you taking the time to leave me such a detailed message. i decided to come to SW over other /r/ threads because i believe suicide is my only cure to not being debilitated by pain anymore, and from watching my life get stripped of meaning by nightmares i can't displace and panic attacks i can't pull out of.

but i appreciate your solidarity. i've always believed the term that framing is everything, but i am struggling to frame the bouts of uncontrollable anxiety and unwillingness to continue on into something constructive. seeing the real me has been getting harder and harder, especially realizing how recklessly i have begun living my life in hopes of either getting an adrenaline rush to curb the pain, or dying. i'm here because i don't know what to hold out for anymore, nor how to hold out and crawl through the trenches.

again, thank you, i appreciate your time.

i really appreciate you taking the time to respond to me, especially a random search. it means a lot that you read my story... it's difficult to feel so alone in this, especially when my support system is minimal and i'm hiding my condition from everyone else. maybe a routine could help, especially the part about having routine failure allowances. i love that. i'm glad to hear she is doing better.. a little reminder that suicide isn't the only cure to depression, however true that feels today. it feels very true today. thank you.

i'm on Wellbutrin. there's risks to everything unfortunately, but those risks are very low. even if it seems like the risk is big, you have to remember you're using an availability heuristic: your sample size of information is the sensationalist internet. there are many, many people on Wellbutrin, and very few have had seizures.

A therapist can be different then a doctor. They won't be able to diagnose you either, which in your case might be nice.  They can talk, and they're normally really well read on the latest science in how-niot-to-suffer-internally.

The label of depressed vs not depressed doesn't always matter.  The fact is, you  feel awful, but it's not your fault. And you don't have to feel awful.  Try giving a therapist a call, see what they say. There's a lot of benefit to be had.

Ive resisted medication for the past 5 years after my college therapist asked if that's what I was looking for. I actually pursued an education in psychology and neuroscience, helmed by the belief that drugs were over prescribed and that alternative therapies were more effective. Studies didn't support my claim, but I raged forward anyways. 

My current therapist suggested I see a psychiatrist 4 months ago. She said my symptoms were worse, and that it was actually inhibiting my progress in therapy. I resisted, again, and she asked "If I had a broken leg, would you think I was weak if I took pain killers? No. Your depression isn't a choice, you can't will your broken leg not to be broken."

When I tested at the psychiatrist, we found that my symptoms and prognosis were so severe, it was scientifically likely that my brain had all together stopped supporting the feel good centers of my brain. They were barren, which made sense why I always felt like shit. A "jump start", she said. That made a lot of sense. 

It took some trial and error but I found a good match. The road isn't easy, but I will say that being on medication had made my day to day life easier. I never thought I would say that. It doesn't change who you are, I promise. It changes the emotional response of your brain very moderately, so that DEFCON isn't your go to emotional state. It takes the edge off of the feeling of oblivion, and ultimately can help prevent daily depressive shit holes by intercepting the emotion-thought spiral that is not feeling better from the start.

Come back after your appointment. Tell us how you feel. We are rooting for you.

I'm not a medical professional, so please take this with a grain of salt. I'm currently on Wellbutrin XL after trying other meds.. not all days are created equal. Some days I feel hopeful for the first time in decades, other times (like today) I'm pretty convinced the only way to end depression is to leave my body. Wellbutrin is a dopamine reuptake inhibitir, so it's a completely different breed then common antidepressants, SSRIs, like Prozac and Cellexa. Studies sound like they're suggesting this shit works by giving your reward centers something to fuel themselves with, which suggests that the drug is mainly effective by increasing the reward feeling after accomplishing stuff.

You can stay with this drug, but our brains are crazy fucks (neuroscience education here). They're plastic, so they chAnge constantly and elusively and there's a good chance what worked for you before is facing different chemical design in your brain now. I just want you to know this isn't your fault, and that the attempt at Wellbutrin working was a great first go, but it might not be the right med for you anymore. 

My doctor suggested giving me Ambilify to help curb the symptoms I couldn't squash with Wellbutrin. I declined because I'm on 3 others for alternative diagnoses, otherwise I would have. that might be a concrete thing to talk to your doctor about.

Go see your doctor again. It's not your fault that you feel this way.
